messages.author: f258cc397470052b
messages.subject: lavSpatialCorrect stopped producing output
parts:
Hi all,

In the recent past I have successfully used lavaan to run a SEM model and then used lavSpatialCorrect to account for spatial autocorrelation. However, lavSpatialCorrect no longer seems to be working for me. Has anyone else had this problem or know of a possible solution?

I have successfully fit a model using the 'sem' lavaan command and get output with the 'summary' command:

> fit <- sem(model, data = data_sem, estimator = "MLM")
> summary(fit, standardized=TRUE)

The output says the model converged normally and all looks reasonable in the output.

However, when I follow up with:


> source(./lavSpatialCorrect.R")
> library(ape)
> lavSpatialCorrect(fit, data_sem$X, data_sem$Y)


The output is only:

$Morans_I
named list()

$parameters
named list()


So, I am not getting the adjusted results.

Thanks all,
Kyle

messages.author: 6b0398f60fd2d0a1
messages.subject: Re: lavSpatialCorrect stopped producing output
parts:
It’s come to my attention that lavaan no longer produces proper residuals. Please don’t use lavSpatialCorrect until this is fixed.  You can calculate residuals yourself manually by now and feed them in, but for the moment, don’t use the function with a lavaan object.


Can it be temporarily disabled in the relevant package?

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: lavSpatialCorrect stopped producing output
parts:
Not in 0.5-22.

You seem to suggest that this is something that is 'broken' in lavaan,
and needs to be fixed, but the fact of the matter is that
resid(,"casewise") was never intended to be used in
observed-variables-only settings, as explained in many posts, including
here: https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/issues/44

It may be difficult to understand for many of you who do not use latent
variables, but predicting the values of observed variables in a full SEM
model (including a structural part) is not trivial *in general*.

Nevertheless, I will study this and see if I can find a solution.

Yves.
